title: The Day Alaska Changed Flags #shorts
summary: The Alaska treaty was signed in Washington on 30 March 1867; on 18 October 1867 the flags were swapped at Sitka; the treaty ran the border up the 141st meridian.
tags: why did the us buy alaska
sources: Treaty with Russia, March 30, 1867 (15 Stat. 539), Article I boundaries: in the east the 1825 Russian-British line, then the meridian of the 141st degree to the Frozen Ocean; in the west a line through Behring's Straits at 65 degrees 30 minutes north, midway between the islands of Krusenstern and Ratmanoff, due north into the Frozen Ocean and south-west through Behring's Sea; Article VI: seven million two hundred thousand dollars in gold; ratified May 28 and proclaimed June 20, 1867 (full text, Alaska State Library): https://library.alaska.gov/hist/fulltext/ASL-KF50.U58v15-p539.htm

Check for the Purchase of Alaska: a $7.2 million check dated August 1, 1868, payable to Russian Minister Edouard de Stoeckl; treaty signed March 30, 1867; the US acquired nearly 600,000 square miles for less than 2 cents an acre; critics called it 'Seward's Folly' (U.S. National Archives, Milestone Documents): https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/check-for-the-purchase-of-alaska

Castle Hill, Sitka: place of the formal ceremony for the transfer of Russian America to the United States on October 18, 1867; the Russian flag was lowered and the United States flag raised (National Park Service, American Flag Raising Site): https://www.nps.gov/places/american-flag-raising-site.htm

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html. The coral treaty lines are drawn approximately from the treaty's wording; the eastern line follows today's boundary.

scenes.narration: On {October 18, 1867|October eighteenth, eighteen sixty-seven}, at Sitka, the Russian flag came down, and the American flag went up.
The treaty had been signed in Washington, that {March 30|March thirtieth}.
It drew the line: up the {141st meridian|hundred and forty-first meridian} to the Arctic, and through the Bering Strait.
